text.p: Thai rescue workers are hunting a crazed bull elephant who trampled two people to death in a northern village, police said on Tuesday.

The 30-year-old, five-tonne elephant killed the villagers after breaking free of his chains in the Hangchat district of Lampang province, about 650 km (390 miles) north of Bangkok, on Sunday, police said.

The elephant's owner had chained it to a tree after the animal went crazy and had then rushed to the nearby village to warn people not to approach the animal. The two killed had not heard the warning, police said.
Police and rescue workers were tracking the elephant in the dense jungle where it had fled.
